title: Ripple-gate batcher and latency leveler for continuous streams
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Problem: In continuous streaming workloads we observe recurrent p95/p99 latency spikes when the runtime switches kernel paths or when attention prefetch jitter aligns poorly with decode bursts. These spikes increase unit cost due to conservative SLO padding and degrade user-perceived latency in chat/streaming flows.

Goal: Implement a low-intrusion admission + shaping layer (the 'ripple-gate batcher') that smooths request ingress, surfaces kernel hints to the scheduler earlier, and applies a gentle decode pacing policy to reduce tail latency without sacrificing throughput or significantly increasing token cost. Target: reduce p99 latency by >= 15% on medium-length streams (avg 80 tokens) and p95 by >= 8%, with <= 2% throughput loss and no >5% increase in tokenized cost for typical workloads.

Scope: runtime-side changes only (admission controller, batch shaping, kernel hint propagation, attention prefetch alignment, decode pacing). No customer API changes. Rollout via canary in the hosted pool followed by Dedicated desks after validation.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout in hosted region shows p99 reduction >= 12% and p95 >= 6% on targeted workloads compared to baseline
No regression on throughput (requests/sec) beyond 2% and no increase in error rate
Kernel selection telemetry shows earlier hinting for >70% of streamed requests
Automated e2e replay tests pass for high-concurrency tail scenarios
Runbook and rollback playbook documented and tested in staging
implementation_plan:
1) Add Ripple-gate admission shim between socket ingress and prefill queue. 2) Implement lightweight entropy bucketing to group similar sequence-length/attention shapes for kernel hinting. 3) Introduce decode pacing token-shedder that enforces micro-delays when tail concentration is detected. 4) Propagate kernel hints to kernel selection module and telemetry. 5) Add feature flag and canary gating with metrics export. 6) Observe, tune thresholds, and iterate.

Engineering notes: keep admission shim non-blocking and lock-free; maintain per-core statistical counters; use existing kernel hint protobuf fields to avoid schema churn.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete. Measured p99 spikes correlated with kernel swap events and attention prefetch misses in 70% of cases in our replay traces.
2026-03-05: Prototype of entropy bucketing implemented; groups sequences into 4 buckets based on length and attention density. Local bench shows 6% reduction in p99 for synthetic stream replay.
2026-03-08: Admission shim integrated; added non-blocking ring buffer and backpressure watermark. Initial canary schedule planned for 2026-03-14 in region us-west-2-hosted-small.
2026-03-11: Decode pacing algorithm tuned to micro-sleep windows of 200-600us; observed tail smoothing but slight throughput dip (~1.4%). Will iterate to reduce cost impact.
test_plan: Unit tests for admission shim and entropy bucketing (coverage >= 85%)
Integration replay tests using production traffic traces in staging: compare baseline vs ripple-gate under identical load
Load tests at varying concurrency (50%, 100%, 200% of expected peak) with kernel-heterogeneous workloads
Grafana dashboards to track p50/p95/p99, kernel-swap counts, admission-drop rates, and token cost per request
Canary run with automated rollback on error rate or latency regression thresholds
metrics_and_targets: Token cost delta for typical streams: <= +5%
Kernel-swap events reduced by >= 40% in canary traces
notes: Trade-offs: stronger shaping reduces tail but can increase jitter for p50; we prefer conservative shaping to protect p99 for interactive users.
If decode pacing causes >2% throughput loss on Dedicated desks, fallback is to enable kernel-hint-only mode while leaving pacing disabled.
Security: no customer data leaves the runtime; kernel hints are derived from sequence metadata only.
Follow-ups: if rollout successful, plan separate ticket to expose a tenant-level shaping knob for Dedicated customers.
